subject: Computer Networking
title: Bandwidth vs. Latency
description: A short lesson to help you apply Bandwidth vs. Latency.

hook.text: Your download is fast but your video call lags. Speed and responsiveness aren't the same thing.

buildup.text: Bandwidth is how much data fits through a connection per second. Think of it as a pipe's width.

discovery.text: Latency is how long a single piece of data takes to travel from A to B. That's the pipe's length.

twist.text: Streaming needs bandwidth. Gaming needs low latency. Different apps care about different things.

climax.text: A satellite link has huge bandwidth but high latency. A fiber link has both — that's why fiber wins.

punchline.text: Bandwidth fills the bucket. Latency decides when.

quiz.question: What does latency measure?
options: The time it takes data to travel from source to destination
The maximum amount of data a connection can carry
The number of devices on a network

details.summary: Bandwidth is how much data a connection can carry per second, measured in bits per second. Latency is the time it takes for a single packet to travel from source to destination. High bandwidth with high latency feels sluggish; low latency matters most for real-time applications.
details.whyItMatters: Bandwidth and latency are the two dimensions of network performance. Confusing them leads to misdiagnosing connection problems and choosing wrong solutions.
takeaways: Bandwidth measures capacity; latency measures delay
High bandwidth does not guarantee low latency
Real-time apps like gaming need low latency over high bandwidth

faq.question: Why can I have fast internet but still experience lag?
faq.answer: You likely have high bandwidth but high latency. Bandwidth determines download speed for large files, but latency determines responsiveness. A connection with 1 Gbps bandwidth but 200ms latency will feel slow for video calls and gaming even though large downloads are fast.

faq.question: What causes high latency?
faq.answer: Physical distance is a major factor since signals travel at the speed of light. Network congestion adds queuing delay. Each router hop adds processing time. Satellite connections have high latency due to distance. Wi-Fi adds latency compared to wired connections.
